script: This is seventeen seconds of phone video. Just me, walking down a hallway. That's all SamWorld needs to build a world.

SamWorld sends twenty-five frames to Meta's MapAnything, running on a GPU worker on Modal. It rebuilds the hallway as a one-million-point cloud, at real scale. Six point eight metres long. Two point three metres high.
Next, SAM 3.1 outlines the objects. Nine of them, doors and doormats, tracked across ten different views. Muse Spark names each one, and lifts it into 3D space.
And this is the result. Your hallway, rebuilt as a 3D world you can walk through. The walls are textured from your own video, and SAM 3D rebuilt the objects as real 3D models, right where they sit.

But here's what makes SamWorld different. You can prompt it to change the location. Type a new place, like a haunted Victorian library, lit by candles. Muse turns that one sentence into a plan for every wall, the floor, the ceiling, and every object it found.
Muse Image, Meta's image model, paints every surface from that plan. Damask walls. Worn oak floors. A smoke-stained ceiling. Every door and every mat is restyled too, and SAM 3D rebuilds them in 3D.

And this is not a picture. You're standing inside the hallway, rebuilt in 3D from that one clip. Walk forward, and the haunted library spreads across the real walls. Now turn around. Every door is carved mahogany, and every mat, a worn Persian rug.

All of this runs on Meta's AI. MapAnything rebuilds the geometry. SAM 3.1 finds every object. Muse Spark understands the room and plans the new world. Muse Image paints it. SAM 3D brings the objects into 3D. And the Immersive Web SDK puts you inside it, in the browser, or on a Quest.
Phone video in. Any place you can prompt, out. In the browser, or on a Meta Quest. SamWorld. Built with Muse, SAM 3.1, SAM 3D, and Modal.
